correctness.rationale: For every \(m\ge3\), the published Theorem 9.5 identifies Y with the isolated-forest model and proves reduced homology concentration in degree m-3. The signed fixed-face Lefschetz formula is reconstructed: g-invariant parent maps descend to cycle orbits with target length dividing source length, exactly lambda_target possible equivariant phases, and quotient cycles are forbidden. Each non-root orbit contributes (-1) after combining simplicial and orientation signs. The directed matrix-tree determinant with signed weights and inclusion-exclusion over forced isolated cycles gives the claimed character, with correct empty determinant and augmentation signs. Actual packaged verify.py was run and produced VERIFY_OK for 30 conjugacy cases and mod-two ranks for \(m=3,4,5\). The general proof does not rely on finite enumeration.

originality.rationale: The source that defines Y (Knudson–Owens–White arXiv:2609.06844 Theorem 9.5) supplies homotopy and Betti ranks but not an S_m character. Broader rooted-forest determinant theory (Bernardi–Klivans) covers the weighted enumeration ingredient but not the cycle-type quotient and isolated-orbit Lefschetz character. Database and literature searches for the same objects, exact action, aliases and reductions found no dominating formulation. The unchecked Kozlov 1999 full text and unindexed equivalents remain residual risks, rather than proof of absence.
residual_risks: Full text of Kozlov (1999) was not obtained; an equivalent isolated-subcomplex character in uninspected material cannot be excluded.
A different cycle-index or equivariant forest formula in unindexed work could imply this result.
The theorem for the canonical subcomplex does not extend equivariantly to the full strong matching complex without additional proof.

value.rationale: The isolated-forest subcomplex is canonical and central to the published simplex-boundary strong Morse matching computation. The formula determines a full rational S_m representation for all m and all conjugacy classes using small exact determinants. It distinguishes nontrivial permutation actions invisible from the existing sphere counts, e.g. for \(m=4\) identity trace 25, transposition trace -3, and 4-cycle trace 1. The motivating symmetry question and uniform all-parameter character give value beyond numerical recomputation or an arbitrary finite slice.
